title: Contracts Manager
Controls Engineer
description:
The Role

We are looking for a Controls Engineer to join our product engineering team and help design, build, and commission microgrids.
You will report to our Chief Technology Officer and work a hybrid work schedule from one of our offices in either Oakland, CA, Santa Monica, CA, Ridgewood, NJ, or NYC.

Key responsibilities will include:
Design, develop, and program PLC-based electrical control systems
Specify, purchase, and troubleshoot control system hardware and instrumentation (field-mounted and panel-mounted instruments)
Read, understand, and develop control system design documents (Functional Specifications, User’s Manual, and engineering reports)
Troubleshoot and resolve any issues related to electrical control systems to minimize downtime and improve operational efficiency
Design and manage site-level microgrid networks and security
Perform risk assessments and implement safety measures to ensure the safe operation of control systems
Collaborate with internal teams, clients, and external vendors as needed to resolve system issues
Support cybersecurity efforts to ensure secure reliant and redundant controls
Learn our microgrid controls and perfect them for each project

The Ideal Candidate
Strong working experience with PLC programming, controls engineering, and various automation systems
Experience with distributed energy resources, including batteries, solar, generators, and switchgear
5+ years of control loop design and switching power supply experience a plus
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to troubleshoot ladder logic of complex control systems
Solid mechanical, electrical, and software interface skills
Great attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously
Continuous learner, staying updated with the latest advancements in control systems technology
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering and 4+ years of experience OR an equivalent combination of skills, education, and experience.
This is a great opportunity to have a long-term impact on a fast-paced, private equity-based growth business. Some of the core virtues embraced by Scales’ employees include:
Do the Right Thing
Act Like an Owner
Hustle
Demand Results
Go Together
Evolve or Disappear

We offer a competitive compensation package and a comprehensive benefits program including medical benefits, paid vacation and holidays, and 401K matching.

About Scale Microgrids
Scale is redefining resilience, with advanced microgrids that go beyond traditional backup power solutions to give businesses the power to adapt and thrive amid all of today’s growing energy challenges. As a vertically-integrated provider of turnkey advanced microgrid systems, Scale combines project design, engineering, and execution expertise with microgrid-as-a-service financing to offer our customers systems that are optimized to deliver maximum value from day one while ensuring ultra-reliable operations and fast time-to-power.
Scale is backed by EQT, a firm with ~$250B in assets, bringing a depth of experience, resources, and capital that will enable Scale to continue pursuing our vision of powering the world with distributed energy. The investment enables Scale to own and operate billions of dollars in distributed generation assets.  To learn more about Scale Microgrids, please visit https://www.scalemicrogrids.com.

About EQT
EQT is a leading purpose-driven global investment organization with EUR 246 billion in total assets under management, divided into two business segments: Private Capital and Real Assets. EQT owns portfolio companies and assets in Europe, Asia Pacific, and the Americas and supports them in achieving sustainable growth, operational excellence, and market leadership. To learn more about EQT, please visit https://eqtgroup.com.

Scale strives to attract and retain a workforce that reflects the composition of our customer base and communities. We are committed to providing a work environment that provides everyone with equal access and opportunity to contribute and drive meaningful outcomes.  We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply and will consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin.

title: Data Center, Senior Project Manager
description:
The Role

We are looking for an experienced Senior Project Manager to join our Project Management Office (PMO) within the Data Center Engineering organization. This role owns end-to-end delivery of natural gas engine and turbine power plant projects—spanning Behind-the-Meter (BTM) on-site generation and Front-of-the-Meter (FTM) grid-connected solutions.
You will be the owner’s primary representative through every project phase: engaging with Market Development before Notice to Proceed (NTP) to ensure clean handovers into execution, directing the Owner’s Engineer (OE) team as your independent technical oversight partner, and driving projects to commercial operation on schedule and within budget. This is a high-visibility, high-accountability role reporting directly to the VP, Data Center Engineering.
This role combines a strong business acumen, stakeholder management, problem-solving, and a builder’s mindset.  You will be at the center of one of the energy industry’s fastest-growing intersections—distributed and grid-scale power for data centers. You’ll manage technically complex, high-impact projects with real accountability, working alongside an experienced PMO team and reporting directly to senior business leadership. You will help drive the expansion of our data center power solutions business, build trusted partnerships, and ensure Scale remains the leader in data center power solutions for mission-critical facilities.
This role is based out of our Ridgewood, NJ headquarters, but could also be located at our NYC, LA, or Oakland, CA offices.  Remote work is acceptable. You need to be prepared to travel up to 35% of the time to project sites, customer facilities, and OEM factories for FATs.

Key responsibilities will include:
Pre-NTP Market Development CoordinationPartner with the Market Development team on go/no-go reviews, site assessments, and feasibility validation before the NTP is issuedStress-test project schedules, equipment assumptions, interconnection strategies, and cost estimates for execution riskEngage the OE and long-lead equipment suppliers during development to validate technology selections and flag procurement lead-time risksCoordinate with Market Development to ensure a formal pre-NTP handover is held, delivering a documented Execution Readiness Report that captures all open items, assumptions, and risk mitigations

Owner’s Engineer CoordinationDirect the OE team as the independent technical oversight function across all project phases, from design review through commissioning acceptanceAssign OE review of all major engineering deliverables (P&IDs, single-line diagrams, equipment specifications, protection relay plans) and manage comment resolution cyclesCoordinate with Contracts Management to ensure OE witnessing of factory acceptance tests (FATs) for key project equipmentDirect OE construction observation visits require written site observation reports, and use OE findings to drive contractor corrective actions and payment milestone confirmationsObtain OE independent verification of all performance test results before issuing the Commercial Operation Date (COD) certification

Project Planning, Execution & CloseoutDevelop and maintain the integrated project management plan: scope, schedule, budget, risk register, QA/QC, and communications baselineServe as Owner’s representative during construction—chair weekly progress meetings, manage RFIs and submittals, enforce QA/QC and HSE complianceManage EPC/EPCM contracts and major equipment supply agreements; evaluate change orders with OE technical input and administer within delegated authorityLead integrated commissioning planning, coordinating OEM startup technicians, BESS commissioning teams, utility representatives, and the OEOwn project budget from NTP through closeout: monthly cost reporting, EAC forecasting, invoice approval, and contingency managementFacilitate structured asset handover to O&M with OE-approved as-builts, OEM manuals, spare parts inventories, and the OE’s Final Technical Report

Stakeholder Management & ReportingPrimary point of contact for data center customers, utilities, ISOs/RTOs, air quality agencies, lenders, and EPC contractorsDeliver weekly project status reports and monthly executive dashboards to the VP, Data Center Engineering; include OE technical findings and open-item trackingManage air permitting (Title V, minor NSR) and utility/ISO interconnection applications; engage OE for technical responses to regulatory and utility information requests

title: Development Engineer
description:
The Role
We are seeking a seasoned Development Engineer with direct experience designing, engineering, and developing the technical components of C&I microgrid and distributed energy resource projects. In this role, you will translate customer resiliency, cost, and sustainability goals into engineered microgrid solutions capable of operating in parallel with the utility and independently in island mode. You will conduct site investigations, negotiate with utilities, navigate AHJ requirements and procedures, and orchestrate a complex set of constraints into a project scope that Scale can contract, construct, and operate.
You will collaborate with internal cross-functional team members within project deal teams, holding yourself to the highest standard of integrity from start to finish. This is not an entry-level design position: you will own the technical strategy for each assigned project, shaping customer solutions that integrate PV, BESS, controls, and generator assets into a complete microgrid or DER system.

This role will report to our Senior Manager, Project & Development Engineering, and will be a hybrid role based out of our HQ in Ridgewood, NJ, or NYC offices.

Key responsibilities will include:
Support Business Development throughout opportunity qualification and proposal development, providing the technical foundation for the customer-facing solution and stepping in for direct, technical customer conversations when needed.
Perform desktop audits and onsite investigations to evaluate electrical and overall site conditions and translate findings into project-specific design constraints while also flagging discovered risks.
Develop microgrid designs, including one-line diagrams, layouts, and bills of material, progressing from initial concept through contract-ready deliverables. Use production modeling tools to optimize solar, battery storage, and generator assets for performance, resiliency, and economic return.
Support RFP responses and contract negotiations as the technical lead of the deal team.
Own utility interconnection strategy.  Engage directly with utility personnel to distinguish requirements that are strictly necessary from those a utility initially assumes are required, challenging impact studies where appropriate to secure the most economical interconnection outcome.
Lead internal and third-party produced detailed engineering deliverables including interconnection, issue for bid and issue for permit drawing sets, sequence of operations and network diagrams.  Oversee innovative custom switchgear designs that integrate Scale's proprietary microgrid control system to enable autonomous operation, specifying and integrating instrument transformers, metering and protective relays.
Support the technical permitting process with authorities having jurisdiction throughout the Northeast, including both discretionary and ministerial approvals.
Advise on major equipment selection for inverters, generators, and battery energy storage systems, balancing performance, cost, and schedule to inform procurement decisions.
Serve as the overall technical owner of assigned projects, flagging risks and proposing engineered solutions backed by thorough desktop and on-site diligence.
Proactively refine the internal tools and processes that keep results accurate and consistent as project volume scales.

The Ideal Candidate
4+ years of experience in the design, development, or construction of power generation, renewable energy, or utility-scale distributed energy resource projects, with a track record of measurable results.
Comfort serving as the primary technical point of contact across business development, customers, utilities, and internal engineering and product teams, with the work ethic to manage several fast-moving projects at once.
Working knowledge of low voltage and medium voltage electrical systems, typically 480V through 34.5kV, along with the switchgear, protection, and control equipment required to operate them safely.
Working knowledge of utility distribution infrastructure, including transformers, reclosers, metering, line and substation protection, and SCADA, sufficient to design sound interconnection strategies and confidently question or challenge utility study assumptions.
Understanding of onsite generation dynamics, including grid parallel and island mode operation, transition types, associated emissions considerations, and the complexities of DER control systems to meet specific operating and economic goals.
Exposure to reciprocating engines or turbines in the 200 kW to 2000 kW range is a plus.
Experience with property development or diligence platforms, such as Paces or Landgate, is a plus.
Working knowledge of and experience with PV modeling tools such as Helioscope and PVsyst.
Experience with AutoCAD, including the ability to build and maintain templates and automations that improve efficiency and consistency across the team.
Familiarity with utilities and AHJs throughout the Northeast is strongly preferred.
Confidence delivering a clear technical recommendation to internal and customer stakeholders even when no perfect option exists.
BS in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, or a related field is required.
Professional Engineer (PE) license in power, or active progress toward one, is preferred.

title: Director, Capital Markets
description:
The Role

This is a front-office investment management and origination role on the Capital Markets team and is a great role for someone looking to play a leadership role at a fast-growing PE-backed business. You'll be instrumental in supporting the growth of our business, financing distributed energy assets, focusing primarily on batteries and microgrids.

This role will work full-time out of our New York office in the Union Square area.

What we offer:

- Opportunity to join a top-notch team of professionals

- Fantastic team environment and collaborative culture

- Competitive compensation package and a comprehensive benefits program including medical benefits, paid vacation and holidays, and 401K matching

Core Responsibilities:

- The candidate will play a key role leading the origination, structuring, and management of various debt, tax equity, and tax credit transfer facilities

- The candidate will be responsible for the implementation of new project development and capital markets transactions in the financial model

- The candidate must be comfortable implementing the relevant terms of the Inflation Reduction Act and One Big Beautiful Bill Act

- Manage and train the junior members of the Capital Markets team

- Act as a trusted partner to internal and external teams, including legal, accounting, project managers, bankers, tax equity investors, etc

- Maintain positive and effective business relationships internally across Scale’s broader business

- Proactively engage with senior leadership on investment issues and business innovation, and their impact on overall business strategy

The Ideal Candidate:

For you to be successful in the role, you should have:

- 8+ years of experience financing or investing in infrastructure or renewable energy projects, including distributed generation

- 3+ years of experience managing analyst- or associate-level financial professionals in a “deal team” structure

- Bachelor's degree (preferably in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, or Engineering); MBA or CFA preferred

- Demonstrated financial modeling competency to evaluate different capital structures across the various debt markets (development capital, commercial bank financing, leveraged finance, mezzanine / Holdco debt)

- Experience leading the negotiating, closing, and documenting of debt and tax equity financings

- Experience developing and auditing complex financial models

- Demonstrated experience originating transaction opportunities

- Working knowledge of off-take arrangements for distributed energy

- Experience conducting project/portfolio due diligence and managing third-party consultants and transaction counsel

- Strong interpersonal skills and ability to effectively communicate information and strategic goals to non-financial people

- Proactive and forward-thinking attitude, creative problem-solving ability, and the ability to “manage up”

- Strong understanding of technical/commercial terms and their impact on projects

title: Inventory/Material Manager
description:
The Role

We are looking for an experienced Inventory Manager to own Scale's inventory management program across our nationwide portfolio of operating energy assets. This individual will establish and maintain accurate, centralized visibility into spare parts and replacement equipment across project sites, warehouses, and third-party storage locations, and will develop the systems, processes, controls, and replenishment strategies required to ensure critical materials are available when needed. This is a key operational role supporting the reliability and performance of Scale's growing fleet.

This role will report to our Senior Director of Procurement. The role is based at our Headquarters in Ridgewood, New Jersey. Key responsibilities will include:

Responsibilities:

- Own inventory management across Scale's nationwide portfolio of operating assets, project sites, warehouses, and third-party storage locations.

- Develop, implement, and maintain a centralized inventory database and tracking system that provides accurate visibility into inventory quantity, location, status, ownership, availability, and movement.

- Establish and maintain inventory control standards, including item master structure, stocking policies, minimum/maximum levels, reorder points, safety stock, and critical-spares requirements.

- Partner with Operations & Maintenance and technical teams to forecast spare-part and replacement-equipment requirements based on the installed equipment base, preventative maintenance schedules, failure history, equipment criticality, and vendor lead times.

- Manage replenishment and purchasing of spare parts and replacement equipment, including urgent and emergency requirements, to minimize asset downtime.

- Maintain traceability of serialized and high-value equipment and manage inventory transfers between project sites, warehouses, and other storage locations.

- Establish cycle-counting and physical-inventory procedures; investigate and reconcile inventory discrepancies and maintain high levels of inventory accuracy.

- Monitor obsolete, excess, slow-moving, and unavailable inventory and recommend disposition, redeployment, or sourcing actions.

- Manage day-to-day inventory relationships and processes with equipment manufacturers, distributors, warehouses, and third-party logistics providers.

- Develop and maintain inventory KPIs and reporting, including inventory accuracy, stockouts, critical-spares coverage, replenishment lead time, excess inventory, emergency purchases, and inventory value.

- Lead continuous improvement of Scale's inventory management systems and processes, including integration with ERP, asset-management, purchasing, and service workflows.

- Coordinate across Procurement, Operations & Maintenance, Engineering, Finance, and project teams to ensure inventory supports reliable operation of Scale's assets.

The Ideal Candidate

- 5-8+ years of progressively responsible inventory, materials management, spare-parts, or related experience, preferably supporting distributed field operations or multiple locations.

- Demonstrated experience owning inventory controls and processes, including item masters/SKUs, stocking policies, min/max levels, reorder points, safety stock, cycle counts, and physical inventory reconciliation.

- Hands-on experience implementing, improving, or administering inventory management, ERP, CMMS, or asset-management system; strong ability to translate operational requirements into a scalable system and database structure.

- Strong analytical and reporting skills, including advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience developing inventory KPIs and management reporting.

- Experience managing inventory across multiple warehouses, project sites, service locations, and/or third-party logistics providers.

- Experience with serialized equipment, high-value components, spare-parts planning, replenishment, and emergency replacement requirements.

- Strong understanding of mechanical and electrical equipment and parts; experience in power generation, renewable energy, utilities, industrial service, field service, or a similar asset-intensive environment is strongly preferred.

- Experience working with equipment manufacturers, distributors, warehouses, subcontractors, and service technicians.

- Excellent organization, communication, and cross-functional coordination skills, with the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced environment.

- A process-oriented mindset with a demonstrated ability to build structure, improve data quality, establish controls, and drive accountability across an organization.

description:

Be comfortable giving thoughtful feedback to your peers and even supervisors.

title: Software Product Manager
description:
The Role
We are looking for a Software Product Manager to build and improve the internal software used daily by teams that design, deploy, and manage microgrids and data center energy solutions. In addition to product development, this person will drive Scale’s internal AI adoption efforts and steer key cybersecurity initiatives.

This is a broad role in a lean team, well-suited for someone with strong PM craft, AI fluency, and the versatility to operate across multiple workstreams. You’ll be close to the product work – from understanding user needs to shipping improvements that matter.

You’ll report to our Staff Product Manager and work a hybrid schedule from our New York City office near Union Square.

Key responsibilities will include:

Lead products from discovery through launch: clarify problems to solve, define and scope features, drive prioritization, and partner with engineering and design to ship
Develop a deep understanding of internal customers and users; continuously refine through direct engagement and research
Maintain a clear, prioritized roadmap and stay proactively ahead across concurrent workstreams, ensuring the team is always focused on the highest-value problems
Make day-to-day product decisions grounded in user research, business context, technical feasibility, and ROI; define and track outcomes, not just outputs
Partner on software strategy; bring forward insights from discovery to inform direction
Manage stakeholder relationships across product areas and functions – including project analysis, business development, asset management, and engineering – running regular touchpoints, setting expectations, and communicating progress and tradeoffs clearly
Leverage AI to increase your own productivity; help drive the incorporation of AI capabilities into our products
Drive Scale’s internal AI adoption – assess how teams across the organization are using or could benefit from AI, prioritize where to provide support, and serve as an internal resource for teams navigating AI tools and workflows
Steer Scale’s ISO certification program alongside external consultants, coordinating across stakeholders and collaborating with IT & Engineering on cybersecurity priorities
Coordinate with other functions for product releases; provide demos and training to users
Contribute to team standards and continuously improve how the PM function operates

The Ideal Candidate

3+ years of product management experience in an early or growth-stage B2B environment, with demonstrated end-to-end ownership of a product
Energized by taking products and making them work better - finding the problems that matter, shipping improvements, and seeing the impact in how users work
Efficient in discovery: able to run lean, effective research in parallel across multiple products; knows when there is enough signal to move forward
Strong analytical, quantitative, and creative problem-solving skills; comfortable making calls with limited data
Strong communication and interpersonal skills; able to manage a range of internal stakeholders and translate between technical and business contexts
Comfortable managing multiple product areas simultaneously, with the ability to context-switch and allocate attention based on where it’s most needed
Comfortable operating in a lean team; self-directed and able to manage competing priorities without heavy scaffolding
Motivated by going deep on a product domain and growing as a practitioner
AI fluency – uses AI tools as a natural part of the work, and excited by the prospect of helping an organization develop its AI capabilities and navigate how to use them effectively
Ability to take on program management or cross-functional coordination responsibilities alongside product responsibilities
Good understanding of software technologies, cybersecurity and development
Enthusiasm for the company’s mission and vision for a distributed energy future
Industry experience in energy, utilities, or closely related infrastructure sectors
Nice to Have: experience with distributed energy resources (e.g., energy storage, PV, microgrids), utility tariffs and rate structures, grid services
Nice to Have: experience with security compliance or certifications (e.g., ISO, SOC 2)
Nice to Have: experience with data center operations or infrastructure

title: Systems Administrator
description:
The Role
We're seeking a Systems Administrator to architect, deploy, secure, and maintain the core systems powering our organization — spanning both corporate IT and the operational technology (OT) behind our deployed microgrids. This dual role blends hands-on engineering with day-to-day administration, with heavy emphasis on access/permissions management, security hardening and compliance (NIST, ISO 27001, SOC 2), network administration, remote connectivity, and monitoring across IT and field OT assets. Strong networking fundamentals are required; hands-on OT/ICS experience in energy, utilities, or renewables is strongly preferred.

This hybrid role will report to our Sr Manager, IT and be based in our HQ in Ridgewood, NJ.

Key responsibilities will include:

Systems Engineering: Design, deploy, and maintain server, storage, and virtualized infrastructure (cloud and on-prem), including Windows Server, Linux, Active Directory/Azure AD, and automation/IaC practices.
Administration: Own identity and access management end-to-end (onboarding/offboarding, role-based permissions, MFA, privileged access, backups, audit logging); apply patches/updates and maintain system health and availability.
Security & Compliance: Serve as primary owner of access governance and least-privilege design; administer EDR, SIEM, MDM, and vulnerability management tools; extend controls into OT (segmentation, secure remote access); support SOC 2/ISO 27001 audit readiness and incident response.
Troubleshooting & Support: Provide Tier 1–3 support across Windows, macOS, Linux, virtualization, and cloud; engage vendors as needed.
Cloud Administration: Manage Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and Azure (VMs, storage, identity, conditional access); implement cloud backup/DR.
Network & Connectivity: Design and maintain switching, routing, VLANs, firewalls, and VPNs; configure cellular modems/gateways for microgrid site connectivity (carrier/APN/SIM provisioning, NAT, failover); build secure IT/OT remote access paths.
OT & Field Systems: Support microgrid controllers, PLCs, HMIs, SCADA, inverters, and meters; troubleshoot protocol-level issues (Modbus, DNP3, MQTT, SNMP, BACnet); partner with Scale’s control team for on-site commissioning and OT patch/firmware management.
Monitoring & Observability: Build and tune monitoring/alerting across IT and OT (health, connectivity, data flow, backups, security events); create dashboards and reduce MTTD/MTTR.
Documentation: Maintain system/network diagrams, SOPs, configuration baselines, and runbooks; generate performance and capacity reports.

The Ideal Candidate

Bachelor's degree in IT, Computer Science, or related field (or equivalent experience); 5+ years as a Systems Engineer/Administrator with direct network administration responsibility.
OT/ICS/SCADA experience in energy, utilities, renewables, or industrial/building systems strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience with NIST, ISO 27001, and/or SOC 2 frameworks.
Certifications preferred: Network+/Security+, CCNA, Azure Administrator, MCSA/MCSE, RHCSA, GICSP, or similar.
Technical Proficiency: Windows Server, Linux (Ubuntu/CentOS), Active Directory, Azure AD, Group Policy, M365; VMware/Hyper-V.
Strong networking fundamentals: TCP/IP, subnetting, routing, VLANs, DNS/DHCP, NAT, firewalls, VPNs.
Hands-on experience with cellular modems/industrial gateways (Cradlepoint, Sierra Wireless, Digi, Teltonika, Peplink) and carrier/SIM management.
Monitoring/alerting tools (PRTG, SolarWinds, Datadog, Zabbix, Grafana); backup/DR platforms (Veeam, Datto).
Familiarity with industrial protocols and IT/OT segmentation; Zero Trust and NIST 800-82/IEC 62443 knowledge a plus.
Strong analytical and communication skills; highly organized and detail-oriented; collaborative, customer-focused mindset
Willingness to travel to office, project, and client sites, including field visits to operating microgrid sites. Approximate travel 25%.
Ability to participate in an on-call rotation and evening/nighttime system migration tasks when required.

title: Project Development Manager
description:
This is a senior individual contributor role with strategic oversight responsibility for leading full lifecycle development of on-site power generation and infrastructure projects to support speed-to-power for hyperscale data centers.

You will originate land opportunities, secure site control, manage interconnection strategy, oversee permitting and commercial structuring, and drive projects to notice to proceed and financial close. This role owns outcomes: it requires strong market knowledge, commercial discipline, regulatory awareness, on-the-ground expertise, and the ability to coordinate internal and external stakeholders without directly managing large teams.

This role will report to our VP, Development – Data Centers, and can be a hybrid role based in Ridgewood, NJ, NYC, Chicago, or West Palm Beach, FL offices.
